Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to send the DPA redlines we're proposing — primarily a few items around subprocessors and runtime data access. High-level asks:

- Explicit prohibition on subprocessors creating persistent snapshots of customer KV cache or inference cache.
- Confirmation that runtime telemetry will be limited to aggregated metrics and that any request-level logs will not include raw customer input or KV values.
- If any telemetry is used for model optimization, we need an opt-out path and explicit "no training" language.

I've attached the annotated redline doc (two pages called out) and a short checklist the procurement team requires before legal will sign. Can you loop in product/security and confirm whether those first two points are acceptable or need engineering exceptions? Procurement is hoping for a yes/no by end of week so we can close the quarter.

Jordan / Grace — quick technical take:

- We do not currently create persistent, customer-specific snapshots of KV cache as a normal operation. The runtime keeps the KV cache in memory and flushes it when sessions end.
- There are two code paths to watch: (a) debug dumps (only enabled in internal debug builds) and (b) optional telemetry export for advanced batching diagnostics. Neither is part of the default hosted flow.

Mitigation options we can propose in contract language:
- "Redwood will not allow any subprocessor to create or retain persistent snapshots of customer-specific runtime KV cache or inference cache. Runtime caches are ephemeral and retained only for the duration necessary to serve requests."
- Technical control: we can add a contractual configuration requirement: disable debug-dump endpoints for customer accounts by default, and require written approval for any diagnostic export.
- For telemetry: provide aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry by default; create an opt-in mechanism for request-level logs strictly for troubleshooting, with customer-controlled retention and redaction (and audit logs).

Effort: the config and default hardening are low (policy + config change). Adding a legal/contract requirement to disable debug dumps for customer accounts is trivial to enforce.

I'll attach a short snippet that legal/Product can use as proposed language.

—Dev

Thanks — this aligns with what I expected. A couple of product-side concerns and suggested tradeoffs for negotiation:

- Impact: disabling any ability to export request-level cache contents reduces our ability to debug cache-related regressions and may increase time to resolution for some customer issues. That has a small cost impact (more manual debugging) but seems reasonable as a standard offering.
- Compromise language we could offer: allow "ephemeral, in-memory cache for serving only; no export or persistent storage of cache content to storage or logs without explicit customer opt-in for troubleshooting, and only under an auditable, time-limited approval."
- Telemetry: we should provide Azura with a telemetry options page in the Console where they can choose aggregated vs. verbose (opt-in) — that'll be an engineering/console ticket but good to offer as a product feature.

Proposed contract clause (short):
"Redwood Inference will not permit subprocessors to persist or export customer-specific runtime cache contents. Runtime caches are ephemeral; any diagnostic export of request-specific cache contents may only occur with the Customer's explicit, time-limited written approval and will be logged and auditable."

If Security is comfortable with this phrasing I can sign off from Product. Also want to understand whether the opt-in telemetry will require changes to the Console for self-serve; if yes, let's create a small RFC and timeline to present to Azura if they request opt-in.

—Grace

All — security input below. Product/Engineering proposed clause looks fine with the following additions that I require before I can give formal sign-off to Legal:

1) Subprocessor roster: we will provide an up-to-date list of subprocessors and commit to notify customers of changes 30 days before onboarding.
2) Encryption & KMS: any stored diagnostic artifact (if ever created under opt-in) must be encrypted using customer-managed keys where feasible; otherwise, strong Redwood-managed KMS with audit logs.
3) Audit & SOC: include a clause granting Azura the right to request SOC 2 Type II reports and to run a limited compliance audit on data handling for a commercial remediation path.
4) No training: explicit line that no customer raw requests, KV cache contents, or outputs will be used to train models without explicit, separate consent.

Suggested final paragraph to add to the DPA: 
"Redwood will not permit subprocessors to persist customer-specific runtime cache contents. Any diagnostic export of request-specific cache contents will only occur with the Customer's explicit, time-limited written approval, will be encrypted at rest using customer-managed keys where provided, and will be auditable. Raw request data and cache contents will not be used for model training without separate customer consent."

If Product & Eng are happy with these additions I'll mark Security as provisionally approved and ask Legal to incorporate. Also suggest we add a short footnote in the Console (if we implement opt-in) summarizing these controls so procurement/legal at customers have visibility.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security & Compliance

Sarah / Azura procurement — thanks for the redlines and patience while we looped in Product & Security. Summary of agreed position and next steps:

- Agreement in principle: Redwood will not permit subprocessors to persist or export customer-specific runtime KV or inference cache contents. Runtime caches will remain ephemeral unless a customer explicitly requests a time-limited diagnostic export.
- Telemetry: default is aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry only. Request-level logs are opt-in, require customer approval, will be auditable, and subject to encryption and retention limits.
- No training: raw request data or cache contents will not be used to train models without separate written consent.
- Subprocessors & audits: we will provide current subprocessor roster and 30 days notice for changes; SOC 2 reports or limited compliance audits are available per standard procurement paths.

Next steps: I have a short clause bundle Hannah & Grace proposed and Dev confirmed is enforceable. Laura from Legal is looped to incorporate these into the DPA. I'll send an updated redline (attached) and the DocuSign link once Legal has finalized — target: updated DPA to you by Friday.
